editionStatus: May 2018; still listed on the current AAST technical-guidelines index
authorityBoundary: Use for technologist capnography setup, acquisition, calibration, signal-quality monitoring, troubleshooting, cleaning, treatment-monitoring context, and documentation. Current AASM Scoring Manual rules control hypoventilation definitions, thresholds, scoring, and required reporting. Keep ETCO2 and TcCO2 distinct because sensor behavior and artifacts differ.
bestFor: End-tidal carbon dioxide monitoring during diagnostic and therapeutic sleep testing, capnography equipment and sensor concepts, calibration, waveform/signal quality, troubleshooting, monitoring, and documentation.

mappingRationale.D2A: Supports capnography equipment, application, calibration, and technical preparation.
mappingRationale.D2B: Supports performance and monitoring of ETCO2 during indicated sleep testing.
mappingRationale.D2C: Supports signal-quality troubleshooting, physiologic cross-checking, cleaning, and documentation.
mappingRationale.D3A: Supports recognition of valid CO2 signal context while AASM rules control adult scoring.
mappingRationale.D3B: Supports recognition of valid CO2 signal context while AASM rules control pediatric/infant scoring.
mappingRationale.D4C: Supports CO2 monitoring and ventilation context when oxygen or therapeutic interventions are used; oxygen administration remains order/facility-policy dependent.

copyrightUse: Use document title, section headings, original summaries, and learning objectives. Do not reproduce substantial procedures, figures, or older scoring-rule text.
